questions.stem: A clean-up step runs `for (String name : names) name = name.trim();` over `List<String> names = List.of(" ann ", "bob ")`, then prints the list. What does it print, and why?

options.text: The names with their spaces, since each pass assigns to a variable that holds a copy of the element's reference
options.says: the enhanced for copies each element into its own variable; assigning to it replaces only that copy

options.text: The trimmed names, since each pass assigns through a variable that stands for the element's place in the list
options.says: the loop variable is not an alias for the list slot; the list is never written

options.text: Nothing: the loop throws UnsupportedOperationException, since List.of returns a list that can't be changed
options.says: the loop never calls set on the list, so the immutable list is never asked to change

options.text: Nothing: the code doesn't compile, since the variable of an enhanced for is implicitly final
options.says: the variable is final only if declared final; assigning to it compiles

origin.section: The Enhanced for Copies Each Element Into Its Own Variable, So Assigning to It Changes Nothing

questions.stem: A scheduler runs `for (int[] day = {1}; day[0] <= 3; day[0]++) reminders.add(() -> send(day[0]));` followed by `reminders.forEach(Runnable::run);`. Which days are sent?

options.text: Days 1, 2 and 3, since each lambda copies day[0] when the lambda is created
options.says: the lambda captures the array reference, not the element's value; it reads day[0] when it runs

options.text: Days 1, 2 and 3, since each pass of the loop creates a new day array for its lambda
options.says: the initializer runs once, so there is one array for the whole loop, shared by all three lambdas

options.text: Day 4, three times, since each lambda reads day[0] when the lambda is executed
options.says: all three lambdas share one array whose element the loop left at 4, the value that failed the condition

options.text: Day 4, three times, since the compiler copies the final value of day[0] into every lambda
options.says: nothing is copied at the end of the loop; each lambda reads the shared element when it runs, which a lambda run during the loop would show

origin.section: A Lambda Can Capture the Enhanced for's Variable, Not the Basic for's Counter

questions.stem: An archiver runs `for (int offset = 2_147_000_000; offset < 2_147_483_000; offset += 1_000_000) archive(offset);`. What does the second call to archive receive?

options.text: 516,352, since the sum wraps past the top of int and counts on from zero
options.says: a wrap keeps the low 32 bits of the true sum, so it lands 2^32 below it, in the negative numbers, not at a count from zero

options.text: -2,146,967,296, since the sum wraps past the top of int into the negative numbers
options.says: 2,148,000,000 does not fit in an int and wraps to 2,148,000,000 - 2^32, which is below the bound, so archive is called again

options.text: 2,147,483,647, since the sum stops at the top of int, Integer.MAX_VALUE
options.says: int addition wraps; it never saturates at the largest value

options.text: 2,148,000,000, since the sum is widened to long once it passes the top of int
options.says: int arithmetic stays int; nothing widens it, and the sum wraps

origin.section: A Loop Ends Only When Its Condition Turns False, and int Overflow Can Keep It True

questions.stem: A replay tool counts frames with `for (float t = 0f; t < 20_000_000f; t += 1f) render(t);`. How many frames does it render?

options.text: 20,000,000, since every whole number from 16,777,216 up to 20,000,000 is a float
options.says: from 2^24 on, adjacent floats are 2 apart, so only every second whole number there is a float

options.text: 20,000,000, since every whole number up to Float.MAX_VALUE, 3.4028235 x 10^38, is a float
options.says: a float's range is that large, but from 16,777,216 on adjacent floats are 2 apart, so not every whole number is a float

options.text: Without end, since t passes Float.MAX_VALUE, 3.4028235 x 10^38, and wraps to a negative value
options.says: t never gets near Float.MAX_VALUE: it stops at 16,777,216

options.text: Without end, since t + 1f rounds back to t once t reaches 16,777,216
options.says: at 2^24 adjacent floats are 2 apart; 16,777,217 lies exactly between two floats and rounds to even, 16,777,216, so t stops below the bound

origin.section: A Floating-Point Counter Changes the Number of Passes, So Count With an int
